Figure 41 displays the speed distribution for each day and road type for combination-unit long- haul vehicles, aggregated over all hours of the day. On rural freeways on weekdays, trucks from FleetDNA data spend 64% of their time in speed bin 14, between 62.5 and 67.5 mph (plotted at 65 mph midpoint). On weekends on rural freeways, trucks spent 70% of their time in speed bin 14. On other roads, we see a less sharp peak at the 65-mph midpoint, with trucks spending only about a third of their time in that bin; we also see a bump of around 7% of driving at speed bin 2 (midpoint at 5 mph). On urban freeways, we see a broader peak around the 65-mph speed bin compared to rural freeways, with trucks driving around 40% the time in that bin as well as near a 52 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. quarter in speed bin 13 (midpoint at 60 mph). Combined speed bin distributions for combination-unit long-haul vehicles For combination-unit short-haul vehicles from FleetDNA and CE-CERT aggregate data on urban freeways, we see a peak at the 60-mph midpoint speed bin on weekdays and a much broader peak from 55 to 70 mph on weekends. On urban other roads, we see the most time spent in speed bin 2 (midpoint at 5 mph) with an additional minor peak at 55 mph. For rural roads on weekdays, results have been shaded with caution due to the hourly data density analysis (refer to Section 4.3); however, when aggregated over hours, there are now 25 and 27 vehicles and 197 and 37 hours of recorded data on freeways and other roads, respectively. While we would still like to see a few more vehicles in these groups to have robust data, of which the lower count may contribute to the less smooth distribution lines, these speed distributions could be incorporated into MOVES if viewed as an improvement due to their source-specific nature over current MOVES defaults. 53 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications.
